citation: Staab, Vero, Balunović and Vechev (2024), Beyond Memorization: Violating Privacy via Inference with Large Language Models, ICLR 2024 (spotlight), arXiv 2310.07298 v2 (HTML read)
text_source: PersonalReddit: 520 Reddit profiles, comments 2012 to early 2016; 1,066 attribute labels with hardness 1 to 5
feature: Personal attributes inferred by an LLM from text with no named identifier; same after Azure Language Service entity removal
method: Nine LLMs (GPT-4, Claude 2, Llama-2 7B and 70B and others) give up to three guesses with reasoning; Azure removes locations, persons, organisations, dates, ages, numbers and currencies
outcome: Top-1 and top-3 attribute accuracy
incremental_to: Human labellers (who could search the web)
pit_handling: Not applicable (inference, not recall); defence test shows residual inference from context
informs_decision: Q3: entity removal does not stop an LLM that reasons from context (GPT-4 85.5% top-1; after Azure 85.0 to 43.9 at hardness 1 but 69.2 to 61.5 at hardness 5); matches EXP-0028/0030; reuse top-3 scoring and hardness labels

citation: Staab, Vero, Balunović and Vechev (2025), Language Models are Advanced Anonymizers, ICLR 2025, arXiv 2402.13846 v2 (v1 titled Large Language Models are Advanced Anonymizers; HTML read)
text_source: Real (PersonalReddit) and synthetic online texts; 13 LLMs as anonymisers; human study with 50 participants
feature: Text rewritten by an anonymiser LLM fed the inferences and reasoning of an attacker LLM, iterated up to five rounds
method: Adversarial anonymisation loop; GPT-4 attacker; utility = mean of GPT-4 judge readability and meaning, BLEU and ROUGE-1; baselines Azure, Dipper paraphrase, self-disclosure abstraction
outcome: Adversarial attribute accuracy; utility score; human ratings
incremental_to: Azure (86.7% to 66.3%, utility 0.76); Dipper; Dou et al. abstraction
pit_handling: Not addressed; anonymiser's own knowledge checked only by a 0/1 hallucination flag in the judge prompt
informs_decision: Q1/Q3: our EXP-0030 loop is this method; GPT-4 reaches 41.6% after five rounds; specific cues go (city 24.6 to 1.3) and coarse ones stay (country 46.1%), as sector stays for us; weaker attackers underestimate leakage, so test with the strongest attacker; meaning falls 0.79 to 0.67 over three rounds

citation: Yang, Zhu and Gurevych (2025), Robust Utility-Preserving Text Anonymization Based on Large Language Models, ACL 2025, arXiv 2407.11770 v2 (HTML read)
text_source: DB-bio celebrity biographies (239 test) and 525 synthetic PersonalReddit comments (207 test)
feature: Text rewritten to minimise re-identification while a downstream classifier keeps its label
method: Privacy evaluator (given the true person, ranks K = 10 candidates and explains the clues) and utility evaluator (given the true label) feed an LLM optimiser for five rounds; GPT-4 backbone; distilled by DPO
outcome: Re-identification success rate among candidates; downstream classification accuracy (BERT, RoBERTa)
incremental_to: Azure, DEID-GPT, self-disclosure abstraction, IncogniText, adversarial feedback (Staab et al.)
pit_handling: Not addressed; both evaluators see the ground truth and the paper does not discuss label leakage into the rewrite
informs_decision: Q1/Q2: utility-aware rewriting keeps more signal at equal re-identification (DB-bio accuracy 96.02 v 92.02 at SR about 53) but on the subtle Reddit task most signal is lost (58.45 to 35.75); tuning a rewriter or template with the outcome in view carries the outcome, so tune on clean or development episodes only

citation: Krčo, Yao, Meeus and de Montjoye (2026), RAT-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Text Anonymization, arXiv 2602.12806 v1 (HTML read, first 100,000 characters)
text_source: Synthetic GPT-4.1 transcripts and chats (100 English, 50 Spanish, 50 Chinese) embedding census-sampled indirect identifiers and one direct identifier
feature: Re-identification risk as the population probability that a match on attacker-inferred attributes is correct
method: GPT-4.1 attacker infers attributes; risk from the Rocher et al. generative model; re-identified if R > 0.2; twelve NER, DP and LLM anonymisers plus the iterative Staab anonymiser
outcome: Share re-identified; BLEU
pit_handling: Not applicable (synthetic people)
informs_decision: Q3/Q4: measure recognition as anonymity-set size in a known population (for S2: S&P 500 companies consistent with a brief), not only as attacker hits; indirect identifiers drive residual risk; iterative anonymisation works only with the exact list of what to protect (2% v 44% easy risk)

citation: Zhou, Mireshghallah and Li (2025), Operationalizing Data Minimization for Privacy-Preserving LLM Prompting, arXiv 2510.03662 v1 (HTML read, first 100,000 characters; ICLR 2026 poster page not opened)
text_source: ShareGPT (176), WildChat (139), MedQA (108), CaseHOLD (110) prompts; nine target LLMs
feature: Minimal disclosure: per sensitive span, retain, abstract or redact, subject to task utility
method: Priority-queue tree search from the most protective profile, relaxing one span at a time until utility passes (correct in 5 of 5 runs, or GPT-4o judge); attacker recovery audit; models also asked to predict the minimum
outcome: Share of spans redacted, abstracted, retained at the minimum; span recovery rate
pit_handling: Not addressed; for multiple-choice tasks the oracle uses the correct answer
informs_decision: Q1/Q2: template design as a minimisation search; stronger models need less (gpt-5 85.7% redacted v qwen2.5-0.5b 19.3%); redaction protects better than abstraction (recovery 2.7-7.7% v 5.6-14.9%); models overshare when asked what they need; oracle must use non-memorised labels

citation: Wu, Wu and Zou (2024), ClashEval: Quantifying the Tug-of-War between an LLM's Internal Prior and External Evidence, arXiv 2404.10198 v2 and v3 (HTML read); a search result lists it in the NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks proceedings (not opened)
text_source: 1,294 questions in six domains with correct and perturbed reference documents (numeric answers times 0.1 to 10; dates shifted; names altered)
feature: Whether the answer follows the document or the model's prior
method: Six models (GPT-4o, GPT-3.5, Llama-3, Claude Opus, Claude Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Flash) answer with and without the document; prior confidence from token probabilities
outcome: Accuracy, context bias, prior bias, context preference rate
pit_handling: Measures the mechanism (parametric knowledge against in-context text), not dated leakage
informs_decision: Q2: with a correct document a strong model rarely keeps a wrong prior (Claude Opus prior bias 0.021), so quote-checked numbers are the safe part; with an altered document Opus resists it most (context bias 0.157), so never give an informed extractor noised numbers; confident priors win where the document is silent

citation: de Montjoye, Hidalgo, Verleysen and Blondel (2013), Unique in the Crowd: The Privacy Bounds of Human Mobility, Scientific Reports 3, 1376 (PMC copy read)
text_source: Mobile-phone traces of about 1.5 million users, 15 months, about 6,500 antennas
feature: Unicity of a trace given p random points at varying spatial and temporal resolution
method: Unicity measured and fitted as a power law of resolution
outcome: Share of users uniquely identified
pit_handling: Not applicable
informs_decision: Q4: coarsening has weak returns (halving resolution cuts identification by 9.3% with four points, 6.2% with ten; 'even coarse datasets provide little anonymity'); remove fields rather than round them

citation: Rocher, Hendrickx and de Montjoye (2019), Estimating the success of re-identifications in incomplete datasets using generative models, Nature Communications 10, 3069 (PMC copy read)
text_source: Census and survey corpora including US (Massachusetts) data, sampled 0.1% to 100%
feature: Per-record probability of population uniqueness and of a correct match
method: Latent Gaussian copula fitted to a sample; closed forms xi = 1 - p(x)^(n-1) and kappa = (1/(n p(x)))(1 - (1 - p(x))^n)
outcome: MAE and AUC of estimated uniqueness; share unique given k attributes
pit_handling: Not applicable
informs_decision: Q4: a code-only risk per brief with the S&P 500 as the population; 15 attributes make 99.98% of Massachusetts residents unique; sampling gives no protection; used by RAT-Bench

citation: Qian, Wang, Peng and twelve others including Lopez-Lira and Tang (2026), LLMs Don't Know What They Know: Benchmarking Temporal Self-Knowledge for Financial Backtesting (FinDendro), arXiv 2611.06808 v1 (HTML read)
text_source: 2,226 dated US facts 1999 to 2026: FRED macro first releases, month-end prices of 50 large companies, Fed decisions; no company documents
feature: Accuracy against self-reported knowledge; effect of a declared as-of date; measured knowledge boundary
method: Four multiple-choice prompts per fact with chance near 0.27; six frontier and open models and three point-in-time families; no Claude model
outcome: Accuracy, claim rate, knowledge boundary by quarter
pit_handling: Subject of the paper: GPT-5 right on 0.61 of facts it disclaims; declared date cuts claims 0.39 to 0.01 with accuracy 0.76 to 0.75; GPT-4o knowledge ends about seven months before its stated cutoff
informs_decision: Q2/Q5: instructions (answer as of a date, use only the text) remove claims, not knowledge, so an extractor's compliance cannot be read off its output; measure the boundary behaviourally and replay only after it

citation: Lopez-Lira, Tang and Zhu (2025), The Memorization Problem: Can We Trust LLMs' Economic Forecasts?, arXiv 2504.14765 v2; sections 5.6, 5.7 and appendix A.7 re-read for this stream (the existing note lopez-lira-2025-memorization-problem.md does not cover section 5.7)
text_source: RavenPack headlines for the Magnificent 7, January 2000 to June 2024 (pre- and post-cutoff); Capital IQ transcripts
feature: One-sentence 'economic logic' of a headline written by GPT-4o without specifics, then masked (GPT-4o mini per Figure 8)
method: Identification prompt ('You are omniscient') for ticker, industry, quarter and year; directional forecast from the economic logic
outcome: Firm, industry and date identification; directional accuracy
incremental_to: Random benchmarks by size decile; masked headlines
pit_handling: Pre- and post-October 2023 windows; post-cutoff samples of 16 to 36 headlines per stock; authors: the procedure shows skill but fails future-invariance
informs_decision: Q1: the closest finance test of extract-then-re-render; pre-cutoff firm identification still AAPL 46.3%, TSLA 27.5%, MSFT 21.6% (Table 10 Panel B); industry 62.4% v 20% chance for FF5 Consumer (Table 12); directional accuracy 50.74% to 58.19% excluding unknowns; text specific enough to forecast reveals identity

citation: Charpentier and Lison (2025), Stronger Re-identification Attacks through Reasoning and Aggregation, arXiv 2510.09184 v1 (HTML read)
text_source: 127 European Court of Human Rights cases from the Text Anonymization Benchmark test split
feature: Infilling of masked identifier spans from background knowledge
method: Retrieval plus Qwen3 4B (instruction or reasoning) infilling; predictions aggregated over span orderings; general and worst-case background knowledge
outcome: Exact-match re-identification of masked spans
pit_handling: Not applicable
informs_decision: Q3: attacker strength matters: worst-case background knowledge 44.7% (instruct, one order) to 57.2% (reasoning, all orders aggregated), Tables 1 and 2; aggregate several attacker samples before reading a recognition rate

citation: Li, Wen and Li (2026), LLM Anonymization Against Agentic Re-Identification (AURA), arXiv 2605.30848 v3 (HTML read in part)
text_source: 53 interview transcripts from the Anthropic Interviewer dataset that an agentic attacker had re-identified
feature: Mask-and-reconstruct rewrite with a privacy scope widened by transcript-specific quasi-identifiers found by a search agent
method: Attackers GPT-5.1, GPT-5.4-mini and Gemini-3-Flash with web search; utility judged by a separate model family on profile, codebook and unit-grid facts
outcome: Re-identifications out of 53; utility recovery rates
incremental_to: Presidio (26/40/27 of 53); Staab et al. anonymiser (11/12/10); one-shot prompts; DP-MLM
pit_handling: Not applicable
informs_decision: Q3: entity removal leaves most re-identifiable; a scope adapted to each document's own quasi-identifiers reaches 0 to 7 of 53 at unit-grid utility 72.0% to 76.1% v 95.6% for Presidio; utility judge from a different family than the rewriter

citation: Utpala, Hooker and Chen (2023), Locally Differentially Private Document Generation Using Zero Shot Prompting (DP-Prompt), Findings of EMNLP 2023, arXiv 2310.16111 v2 (abstract read)
text_source: IMDB and Yelp reviews
feature: Zero-shot paraphrase by an LLM with sampling temperature as the privacy dial
method: ChatGPT (gpt-3.5) and six open models up to 7B paraphrase; static and adaptive author-identification attackers
outcome: Author identification F1; sentiment F1
pit_handling: Not applicable
informs_decision: Q3: paraphrase hides authorship (author F1 down 46% static, 26% adaptive) while keeping sentiment F1 on IMDB; an adaptive attacker recovers half the loss, so test attackers that see rewritten text

citation: Frikha, Walha, Nakka, Mendes, Jiang and Zhou (2024), IncogniText: Privacy-enhancing Conditional Text Anonymization via LLM-based Private Attribute Randomization, arXiv 2407.02956 v2 (NeurIPS 2024 Safe GenAI workshop; abstract read)
text_source: Texts with eight private attributes (setting not read)
feature: Rewrite conditioned on a decoy attribute value so the attacker is misled
method: Adversarial inference fed to the anonymiser; distilled into LoRA parameters of an on-device model
outcome: Private attribute leakage; utility
pit_handling: Not applicable
informs_decision: Q3: misleading the attacker (a decoy value) cuts leakage by over 90% across eight attributes; for S2 a decoy cannot be used on fields the forecast needs, but it is the published form of our wrong-identity positive control

citation: Liu, Wei, Shi, Li, Zhang, Dhillon and Mei (2025), ExAnte: A Benchmark for Ex-Ante Inference in Large Language Models, arXiv 2505.19533 v1 (abstract read; the arXiv page lists no venue, a search result lists ACL Anthology 2026.eacl-long.72, not opened)
text_source: Stock prediction, Wikipedia events, scientific publications and time-restricted QA
feature: Leakage rate: use of post-cutoff knowledge when told to respect a cutoff
method: GPT, Gemini and Claude models under several prompting strategies
outcome: Leakage rate with a quality score
pit_handling: Subject of the paper: models frequently fail to respect instructed cutoffs
informs_decision: Q2: an instruction to ignore later knowledge does not stop its use; the extractor's 'answer only from the text' is not a safeguard

citation: Li, Schneider, Yu and Gupta (2023), Reidentification Risk in Panel Data: Protecting for k-Anonymity, Information Systems Research 34(3), 1066-1088 (abstract read on RePEc)
text_source: Two marketing purchase panels, 15 consumer goods categories
feature: Record-linkage risk from longitudinal purchase histories; sno-unicity
method: Risk measurement; graph-based minimum-movement k-anonymisation (k-MM) with l-diversity
outcome: Share of panelists at high risk; distortion of marketing metrics
pit_handling: Not applicable
informs_decision: Q4: 17% to 94% of panelists at high risk and unicity understates risk in panels; S2 replays the same companies over many quarters, so linkage across episodes adds risk that a per-episode test misses

citation: de Montjoye, Radaelli, Singh and Pentland (2015), Unique in the shopping mall: On the reidentifiability of credit card metadata, Science 347(6221), 536-539 (abstract read on MIT DSpace)
text_source: Three months of credit-card records for 1.1 million people
feature: Unicity from spatiotemporal points and price
method: Unicity under coarsening of place, time and price
outcome: Share uniquely re-identified
pit_handling: Not applicable
informs_decision: Q4: four points re-identify 90%; price raises risk by 22% on average; coarse data give little anonymity; amounts (like our growth rates) are identifying

citation: Sánchez, Martínez and Domingo-Ferrer (2016), Supplementary materials for 'How to Avoid Reidentification with Proper Anonymization', comment on de Montjoye et al. (2015), arXiv 1511.05957 v2 (abstract read)
text_source: The credit-card setting of de Montjoye et al. (2015)
feature: Formal anonymisation (privacy models) instead of ad hoc coarsening
method: Alternative anonymisation of the data with released algorithms
outcome: Unequivocal re-identifications; analytical utility
pit_handling: Not applicable
informs_decision: Q4: counterpoint: a privacy model applied to the joint record (k-anonymity style) reduced unequivocal re-identifications to zero with more utility than ad hoc coarsening; supports anonymising the whole brief as one record

citation: Alessa, Somane, Lakshminarasimhan, Skirzynski, McAuley and Echterhoff (2025), Quantifying Cognitive Bias Induction in LLM-Generated Content, AACL 2025, arXiv 2507.03194 v2 (abstract read)
text_source: Summarisation and news fact-checking inputs; a self-updating dataset
feature: Framing (sentiment change against the source), hallucination after cutoff, primacy
method: Five LLM families; 18 mitigations; human purchase study
outcome: Rates of sentiment change and hallucination
pit_handling: Hallucination on 60.33% of questions after the knowledge cutoff
informs_decision: Q2: summaries changed the source's sentiment in 26.42% of cases, so an LLM's tone or outlook judgement is not neutral even without hindsight; keep judgements on menus and test them separately

citation: Kim, Muhn and Nikolaev (2023), Bloated Disclosures: Can ChatGPT Help Investors Process Financial Information?, arXiv 2306.10224 v4 read (main text and Appendix D); withdrawn in v5 (9 October 2025) after a failed replication
text_source: MD&As (1,790) and earnings calls (8,537), fiscal 2009 to 2020; 2022 out-of-sample (221 MD&As, 552 calls)
feature: Sentiment of GPT-3.5-Turbo summaries against sentiment of the raw text
method: Unconstrained summarisation prompt; regressions with fixed effects
outcome: Abnormal return over days 0 to 1
pit_handling: Sample overlaps the model's training; a 2022 post-cutoff test reported (summary sentiment 0.144, SE 0.018 v raw 0.073, SE 0.020 for calls); no test of hindsight carried by the summary
informs_decision: Q1/Q2: the one finance case of a rewriter whose output is scored, with a post-cutoff check; carries no weight because the paper was withdrawn

citation: Underwood, Nelson and Wilkens (2025), Can Language Models Represent the Past without Anachronism?, arXiv 2505.00030 v1 (abstract read)
text_source: Historical writing samples
feature: Period-faithful text from prompted and fine-tuned models
method: Prompting with period examples; fine-tuning; automated and human judges
outcome: Distinguishability from real period text
pit_handling: Prompting a current model does not reproduce a period's perspective; fine-tuning fools an automated judge but not humans
informs_decision: Q2/Q5: telling a modern model to write or judge as of the past does not remove later knowledge; pretraining on period text may be needed

citation: Zhang, Chen and Stadie (2026), All Leaks Count, Some Count More: Interpretable Temporal Contamination Detection and Mitigation in LLM Backtesting (TimeSPEC), arXiv 2602.17234 v2 of 25 May 2026 (HTML read in part; stream 08 triaged v1)
text_source: Rationales on Supreme Court cases, NBA contracts and within-sector stock rankings
feature: Atomic claims dated and labelled leaked or admissible; Shapley-weighted leakage
method: Claude Sonnet 4 extracts claims; Gemini 2.0 Flash Lite and Perplexity search date them; regenerate; closed-world aggregator answers only from audited claims
outcome: Decision-critical leakage rate; task accuracy
incremental_to: Temporal hint, self-correction, temporal RAG (stock DCLR 26.0%, 10.3%, 73.3% v 12.2% for TimeSPEC on Qwen3.5-35B)
pit_handling: Leakage blocked, not removed; the labelling models' own cutoffs are not discussed; no human validation of labels in the text read
informs_decision: Q2: the closest design to quote verification, applied to reasoning: answer only from verified claims; the auditing models are themselves informed and unvalidated; v2 numbers differ from the v1 numbers in stream 08

citation: Merchant and Levy (2026), Forecasting With LLMs: Improved Generalization Through Feature Steering, arXiv 2606.27199 v2 (abstract read)
text_source: Forecasting prompts in several domains
feature: Sparse-autoencoder features for time-aware and look-ahead reasoning
method: Steering internal features of the forecasting model
outcome: Look-ahead bias on forecasting prompts; general reasoning
pit_handling: Amplifying time-awareness features reduces look-ahead bias; steering look-ahead features has no measurable effect
informs_decision: Q5: needs model internals, so not available for a commercial roster model; no bearing on template design

citation: Ye, Dineen, Zhu, Lu, Song and Zhou (2026), Hindcast: Replaying Prediction Markets to Evaluate LLM Forecasters, arXiv 2607.14051 v1 (abstract read)
text_source: Resolved Polymarket markets and a frozen Reddit snapshot
feature: Forecasts graded as of a chosen past date with retrieval restricted to earlier posts
method: Per-market cutoff on the retrieval corpus; scored against outcome and market price
outcome: Forecast accuracy against outcome and market
pit_handling: Closes retrieval leakage only; parametric knowledge of newer models is named as a problem, not removed (per abstract)
informs_decision: Q5: a point-in-time retrieval corpus is necessary but not sufficient; it does not address what the model already knows
